items.problem: The bootstrap omitted csproj-linked shared source and content files.
items.evidence: session-log turn 2 copied 9 files and no scenario XAML; NumberFormatting.csproj declares linked App/MainPage code, eight XAML resources/pages, styles, and seven assets. The improved fixture resolves 21 linked items.
items.skill_search: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 Get-ChildItem $Source -Recurse; no Include/Link project-item resolution existed.
items.root_cause: The bootstrap treated physical containment under -Source as the complete project inventory.
items.proposed_fix: Parse explicit Compile/ApplicationDefinition/Page/Content/resource Include and Link entries, expand common project path properties, and copy linked files to their logical Link paths before namespace rewrite and triage.
items.generalizes: Legacy UWP projects frequently share XAML, code, resources, and assets through linked csproj items outside the project directory.

items.problem: The migrated shell changed from the original dark SplitView/ListBox shell with footer links to a light NavigationView shell with a Settings item and no footer.
items.evidence: discrepancies.json all-features layout item; baseline and candidate screenshots; session-log turn 10 authored NavigationView after fetching the navigation anchor.
items.wrong_text_if_any: The SDK-sample MainPage + ListView + Frame idiom was mapped to NavigationView + Frame.
items.root_cause: The shell guidance contradicted the no-redesign principle and overlooked that SplitView, ListView, and Frame are supported in WinUI 3.
items.proposed_fix: Require preservation of supported shell controls, resources, footer content, and links; reserve NavigationView adaptation for a source NavigationView or an actually unsupported shell.
items.generalizes: Shell modernization changes visible hierarchy, theme, automation, and viewport in any migration whose UWP controls still have WinUI 3 equivalents.

items.problem: Large scenario headings extended beyond the right edge.
items.evidence: discrepancies.json all-features heading layout item and the Unicode Extensions candidate screenshot.
items.skill_search: SKILL.md fidelity and shell sections contained no explicit wrapping/sizing invariant and the shell table promoted a different host.
items.root_cause: The replacement NavigationView header consumed different width and did not preserve the source shell's wrapping behavior.
items.proposed_fix: Add a visual-layout invariant requiring long headings to wrap or scroll within the initial window and preserving source sizing behavior.
items.generalizes: Desktop title bars and replacement navigation panes commonly reduce available width and expose latent clipping across migrated apps.

items.problem: All seven scenario outputs were below or partially clipped in the visible viewport.
items.evidence: discrepancies.json: Percent/Decimal/Currency output below viewport; Number Parsing/Rounding/Numeral/Unicode output partially clipped. migration-score.json marks all seven features partial for this reason.
items.skill_search: SKILL.md had no scroll-boundary/available-viewport invariant; source generated XAML placed each action and output inside a ScrollViewer.
items.root_cause: The replacement shell added title/header/status regions and reduced scenario space without preserving the source page's effective scroll boundary.
items.proposed_fix: Require preservation of each page's ScrollViewer boundary and prohibit new fixed rows that place actions or output outside the scrollable region.
items.generalizes: Additional desktop chrome and replacement shells routinely reduce content height; long forms and generated output must remain reachable.

items.problem: The documented final build command failed because winapp has no build subcommand.
items.evidence: session-log turn 29: 'build' was not matched; the installed CLI help listed no build command.
items.skill_search: SKILL.md Step 3, build command discipline, and final build all said winapp build.
items.wrong_text_if_any: Prefer winapp build; After PASS, do a final winapp build.
items.root_cause: The skill conflated winapp launch/package operations with compilation.
items.proposed_fix: Use dotnet build <path-to-csproj> for compilation and retain Test-AppLaunch.ps1 for launching.
items.generalizes: Every migration using the current winapp CLI will hit the same deterministic command failure.
